method.canonical_roundoff_diagnostic: The absolute-voltage Hines replay is retained and compared with the perturbation replay at every timestep; it is not used as the primary denominator for tiny PRIMA errors.
method.pulse_sampling: The exact same 10-pA rectangular current protocol is sampled at each timestep using the end-of-step backward-Euler convention.
method.reduced_solver: Order-168 seven-port and dual-q25 nine-port PRIMA models, same fixed continuous-time projection for all timesteps; reduced backward-Euler systems are refactorized for each dt.
method.reference: Full Hines implicit backward-Euler cable solve; the stable reduction comparison uses a second equivalent Hines replay in perturbation coordinates (zero initial perturbation, zero leak source).
method.temporal_convergence: Full-Hines perturbation traces at 0.1 and 0.05 ms are compared with the 0.025-ms full-Hines trace sampled at identical end times.

research_question: Does the seven-port versus dual-q25 nine-port transient error ratio converge as the backward-Euler timestep is refined from 0.1 to 0.025 ms?
scientific_limits: Only two checksum-pinned individual passive linear-RC morphology reconstructions; not a population.
The 0.025-ms Hines solution is a temporal reference, not an exact continuous-time solution.
The PRIMA projection basis and order are held fixed across timestep values; this isolates transient integration sensitivity, not basis optimality.
Large relative nine/seven ratios are reported with absolute NRMSE and error norms.
No active conductances, synapses, plasticity or biological validation are included.
Full Hines remains canonical. No production solver code or defaults are changed.
